record.original_question: Let P be a bounded projection on L1 whose range is a complemented subspace of L1 and suppose P is non-Dunford-Pettis, equivalently its range is not Schur in the formulation given by the source. Must P be an Enflo operator, meaning that P fixes a copy of L1; equivalently, is every non-Schur complemented subspace of L1 isomorphic to L1?

evidence.quote: An operator T in L(Lp,Y), 1 <= p < infinity, is called an Enflo operator provided T fixes a copy of Lp.
Problem 2 ([45], [14] and [7]). Must a non-Dunford-Pettis projection P in L(L1) be an Enflo operator? Equivalently, whether each non-Schur complemented subspace of L1 is isomorphic to L1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the real (or complex) Banach space $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$. Recall the following definitions.

• A bounded linear operator $T$ between Banach spaces is called Dunford–Pettis (or completely continuous) if it maps weakly null sequences to norm null sequences.
• A Banach space $X$ has the Schur property if every weakly null sequence in $X$ is norm null; equivalently, the identity operator on $X$ is Dunford–Pettis.
• A closed subspace $Y \subseteq L_1$ is called complemented if there exists a bounded linear projection $P: L_1 \to L_1$ with range $Y$.
• A bounded operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(L_1, Y)$ is said to fix a copy of $L_1$ if there is a closed subspace $Z \subseteq L_1$ isomorphic to $L_1$ such that $T$ restricted to $Z$ is an isomorphism onto its image. Such an operator is called an Enflo operator.

Note that a projection $P \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ is non-Dunford–Pettis if and only if its range $P(L_1)$ fails the Schur property.

Question: Must every non-Dunford–Pettis bounded projection $P \in \mathcal{L}(L_1)$ be an Enflo operator? Equivalently, is every complemented subspace of $L_1$ that fails the Schur property isomorphic to $L_1$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem in the isomorphic theory of L_1: whether every non-Schur (equivalently, non-Dunford–Pettis-projection) complemented subspace of L_1 is isomorphic to L_1. Searches yield related literature on Dunford–Pettis and Schur properties, but no resolution of this specific question; it continues to be cited as open in surveys on the structure of L_p-spaces.
